messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#619] Remote R access to a cluster running RHadoop
parts:
Yes, you need to configure Hadoop to work that way and rmr2 will pick up that configuration. How this is accomplished exactly depends on your Hadoop distribution but it boils down to two things: you desktop needs to have Hadoop installed; the configuration "points" to your cluster, providing the necessary server names or addresses and ports. Please refer to the installation instructions of whatever Hadoop distribution you are using. If you can run hadoop jobs from the command line, you should be able to run them also with rmr2, as long as the two environment variables, HADOOP_CMD and HADOOP_STREAMING are properly set, something you have done already for your test run and you should repeat on your desktop. Keep in mind that if your desktop is a windows machine, windows support has just been announced by Hortonworks and we are not able to support rmr2 on windows yet.


Antonio


On Tue, Mar 5, 2013 at 2:27 AM, Nicolas Seyvet <nicolas...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi,

Our cluster is composed of 6 slaves + 1 master.  I can run simple R scripts on the master node in the cluster that use rmr:

library(rmr2)

small.ints = to.dfs(1:1000)
mapreduce(
    input = small.ints,
    map = function(k, v) cbind(v, v^2))

The above seems to work, a job is created, ran on a slave and a result is produced.

Now, my next step would be to setup a remote access to RHadoop on this cluster.  In other words, what would I need to do to be able to run RHadoop from my desktop towards this RHadoop ready cluster?  Is it even feasible?

Thanks
/Nicolas


--

Hey, Antonio,
I'm facing similar problem.
In my Eclipse, I have codes to SSH to remote Hadoop cluster using JSch,

conn.connect();
boolean isAuthenticated = conn.authenticateWithPassword(username, password);
if (isAuthenticated == false)
throw new IOException("Authentication failed.");
Session sess = conn.openSession();
sess.execCommand("R CMD BATCH --no-save --no-restore /usr/local/R/debug.R /usr/local/R/whathappened.txt");

And following is debug.R

library("rmr2")
library("rhdfs")
hdfs.init()

Loading required package: stringr

Error : .onLoad failed in loadNamespace() for 'rhdfs', details:

  error: Environment variable HADOOP_CMD must be set before loading package rhdfs
Error: package/namespace load failed for 鈥榬hdfs鈥?
Execution halted

Turns out rmr2 could pick up right configuration, but rhdfs failed. 

My envs in /etc/profile as following:

JAVA_HOME=/usr/local/java/jdk1.7.0_15
PATH=$PATH:$HOME/bin:$JAVA_HOME/bin
JRE_HOME=/usr/local/java/jdk1.7.0_15/jre
PATH=$PATH:$HOME/bin:$JRE_HOME/bin

export JRE_HOME
export PATH


#Hadoop environment set
export HADOOP_HOME=/usr/lib/hadoop
export HADOOP_CONF_DIR=/etc/hadoop/conf
export HADOOP_CMD=/usr/bin/hadoop
export HADOOP_STREAMING=/usr/lib/hadoop-0.20-mapreduce/contrib/streaming/hadoop-
streaming-2.0.0-mr1-cdh4.3.0.jar
export JAVA_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/hadoop/lib/native

Any suggestion to fix this? I'm quite new to Linux, even have no clue what should I do.

messages.author: 3a4d28884b6fc727
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#619] Remote R access to a cluster running RHadoop
parts: Try setting the environment variables in the Renviron file on the Hadoop machine (http://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-patched/library/base/html/Startup.html).  I ran into some issues where the environment variables from the shell were not visible once in the R session.  The Renviron file provides a neutral way to set environment variables independent of the OS and shell.
